The Croatian–Carantanian War (Hungarian: Horvát–karantán háború; Croatian: Hrvatsko-karantanski rat; Slovene: Hrvaško-karantanska vojna) was a military conflict between Carantania, a vassal of Henry IV, and the Kingdom of Croatia, more precisely Ban Zvonimir, who was supported by the Kingdom of Hungary.
The war began with a Carantanian invasion of Croatia, led by Ulrich I. Ulrich successfully occupied parts of eastern Istria, Kvarner, and parts of Primorje.
Zvonimir, seeing that he could not rely on the support of King Petar Krešimir IV, sought assistance from the Hungarian royal court. Together, the coalition successfully defeated the invading forces and reestablished Croatian authority in the previously mentioned areas.
Background
In 1063 or 1064, sometime after the German invasion of Hungary, Ulrich I, Margrave of Carniola, was granted the lands of Istria by Henry IV. Ulrich took advantage of Croatia’s internal problems and marched against the Kingdom of Croatia.
Carantanian invasion
Ulrich I, Margrave of Carniola, invaded the Kingdom of Croatia. Petar Krešimir IV, who was king of Croatia at the time, was too occupied with internal problems to wage war, so responsibility was given to Ban Zvonimir. The might of the Carantanian forces proved too much for the ban, and Ulrich I successfully occupied lands in eastern Istria, Kvarner, and parts of Primorje. Soon after the occupation, Ulrich I created the "Mark of Dalmatia", which consisted of the occupied regions and likely functioned as a military province.
Allied liberation
Seeing that he was no match for the Carantanian army and that he would receive no support from the king, Zvonimir sent a messenger to his Hungarian allies. Fortunately for Zvonimir, King Béla I and his nephew Géza had finally made peace and were quick to assist him in his struggle. With their combined forces, the Carantanian army was defeated, and the occupied areas were once again brought under Croatian authority.
Aftermath
As a token of gratitude, the Hungarian royals were gifted large amounts of silver, fabrics, and gold, as stated in the Chronicon Pictum: "The king and the prince received royal gifts, precious fabrics, and much gold and silver."
